findings.description: The plan conflicts on JS/TS handling: F003 explicitly names TypeScript/TSX and JSX as heuristic-only tier-1 languages, while F005 requires JS/TS fixtures to remain parser-backed covered/high and F004 guards the existing tier-2 set as the Python crawler plus dashboard JS crawler. The operator must pin whether the existing JS extractor covers JS only, JS/JSX, or JS/TS/TSX before implementation, otherwise the same TS fixture could be required to be both heuristic-low and parser-covered.

Per-language status includes not_found, but the proposed acceptance criteria never define which languages should appear as not_found versus being omitted entirely. F005 says empty_repo must have an empty per-language map, which is reasonable, but that leaves the not_found language state unpinned and potentially untestable in the operator-facing coverage block.

The objective asks for an explicit low-confidence note for unextracted languages, but the plan only guarantees that note for detected languages without tier-2 parser extractors. There is no stated fallback behavior for repos whose language is not in the detector marker table, so an arbitrary uncommon-language repo could degrade to generic filesystem coverage without an operator-facing explanation that language dependency extraction was not attempted.

The plan requires coverage to be computed both on project registration and inside build_view_state, but only F005 clearly mandates the real project-registration plus build_view_state path for fixture assertions. It does not pin that registration-time coverage and build_view_state coverage are identical for the same repo/profile, which could let two divergent code paths satisfy different tests.
